narrative: Public-report paraphrase: Contract workers opened a flange connected to an active process containing pressurised flammable hydrocarbon. A release ignited. The work was a first break, the operator was not present, and the crew had not applied locks or tags to the isolation valves.

Public-report paraphrase: Workers selected the wrong flange while locating an isolation blind. Hydrogen sulfide began leaking as bolts were removed; the flange burst open and released toxic gas. Equipment identification and control markers were inconsistent.

Public-report paraphrase: An independent verifier could not see a valve position because a locking device covered the operator. Instead of stopping work and notifying a supervisor, the verifier assumed the position and signed the verification record.

Public-report paraphrase: An electrician received a severe electric shock during refurbishment because the electrical supply had not been properly isolated. Investigation found no management system for checking electrical-work precautions.

site: Hanford Waste Receiving and Processing Facility
narrative: Public-report paraphrase: During a zero-energy check, an electrician found a pressure switch still energised at 110 volts. The complex lockout/tagout had been misinterpreted, but the check found the condition before workers were exposed.

Guidance-derived positive-control test case: Before work near electrical equipment, the competent person used a suitable isolator, locked it off, checked that the circuit could not be fed by another source, and proved the circuit was no longer live before work started.
